exposure: timing of hemorrhage-control device placement (quantitative blood loss 1,000-1,499 mL vs 1,500 mL or more)
outcome: quantitative blood loss after device placement
rate of packed red blood cell (RBC) transfusion
use of 3 units of packed RBCs or more
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 666 women who experienced postpartum hemorrhage and received either an intrauterine balloon tamponade or a vacuum-induced hemorrhage-control device within a multicenter hospital system.
finding: Transfusion and blood loss after device placement were similar between intrauterine balloon tamponade and vacuum-induced hemorrhage-control devices, but earlier placement of either device significantly reduced device failure and the need for transfusion.
